component.name: Jubler
component.summary: Sync and edit subtitles to video

description.p: Jubler creates, edits and converts text-based subtitles. It reads more than twenty formats, from SubRip and Advanced SubStation Alpha to WebVTT and TTML, and writes back into any of them, so a file prepared for one player can be handed to another.

Timing is done against the film itself. An mpv-backed preview plays the video with the subtitles over it, while an audio waveform and the video key frames show where speech and shots actually begin and end, so lines can be placed on them directly.

ul.li: Two-point synchronisation, time shifting and frame rate conversion
Splitting and joining, of single entries and of whole files
Spell checking with dictionaries downloaded on demand
Quality validation, including the TED guidelines
Character and paragraph styling for the formats that carry it
Subtitle search and download from several providers
Import of the text subtitles embedded in video files
External command-line tools (speech recognition, sync) run on the open subtitles

screenshot.caption: Subtitle table with styling and character-level formatting
Video preview and audio waveform side by side
Vertical layout with the subtitle list beside the preview
Spell checking with Hunspell and downloadable dictionaries
Machine translation of a subtitle range

description.p: Video preview, frame preview, audio waveform and media metadata now run on VLC, replacing MPlayer and ffmpeg. Apple Silicon is supported natively, and external command-line tools such as AI transcription or subtitle sync can be run against the open subtitle, audio or video.

Adds WebVTT alongside the XML-based ITT, TTML and DFXP formats, and a set of command-line tools for automated workflows. The preview gains snapping and modifier keys, the table shows characters per second, and a dark theme arrives together with a unified preferences system that can be imported, exported and reset.
Redesigns the interface for HiDPI displays, with a scaling factor that can be set by hand. Automatic translation through Azure returns, and YouTube subtitles are supported.
